sourcedFrom: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" (UNKNOWN — no copyright line is printed anywhere in the document)
cleanIntro: One book covers two rifles that are not the same rifle. Savage sells the AXIS I with a standard trigger and the AXIS II with an AccuTrigger, prints them together, and says so on its own contents page: SECTION 4 is marked "(Axis II ONLY)". This guide is the AXIS II, so Section 4 applies to you — and the flat warning that the AXIS I trigger is not adjustable does not. Everything else in the book is common to both. The field strip itself is short and entirely mechanical: the bolt comes out through the receiver with the trigger held back and the bolt release pressed, and the barrelled action lifts out of the stock on two Allen screws. Past that Savage stops you: the bolt assembly is not to be taken apart, and it is serial-matched to the receiver it came out of. Read the four digits by the extractor before it goes back in.

steps.title: Unload the Axis II — safety back, bolt back, magazine out
steps.action: Move the safety fully rearward to FULL SAFE, then lift the bolt handle and draw it back to extract whatever is in the chamber, and only then push the magazine release tab on the underside of the stock rearward and pull the detachable box magazine clear. That order matters on this rifle: the Axis feeds from a detachable box, so dropping the magazine first still leaves a chambered round the bolt has not yet lifted out. The tab is at the bottom of the stock ahead of the trigger guard and it moves rearward, not down. Catch the magazine — it drops free once the latch releases.
steps.prose: The Axis safety is a two-position button, so FULL SAFE here still lets the bolt open. That is the design, not a fault.
steps.quote: With the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, move the safety fully rearward to the FULL SAFE position (see FIGURE 1). 2. Lift the bolt handle and pull fully rearward, extracting the cartridge from the chamber. 3. Push the magazine release tab on the bottom of the stock rearward (see FIGURE 9), grasping and pulling the magazine clear of the stock.
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Unloading Your Rifle, p.10
steps.warn: Chamber first, magazine second. A dropped magazine proves nothing about the chamber.

steps.title: Look into the chamber and put a finger in it
steps.action: With the bolt back and the magazine out, look down into the open receiver and then feel the chamber mouth with a finger. Savage's own instruction is not to trust the extractor, and on a bolt gun that is a specific mechanical warning: a case with a torn or slipped rim can stay in the chamber while the bolt travels back looking as though it cycled. Rimlocked or not, the only proof is your eye and your finger on the chamber itself. Do it in that order, every time, before the rifle goes on its side for the strip.
steps.quote: LOOK AND FEEL! BE SURE THE CHAMBER IS EMPTY -- DO NOT TRUST THE EXTRACTOR -- DO NOT ASSUME!
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Unloading Your Rifle, p.10
steps.warn: The extractor is not evidence. Eyes and finger.

steps.title: The Axis safety is TWO position — and the bolt still opens on safe
steps.action: Pull the safety button rearward until the red dot is covered and understand what that does and does not do on this rifle. On the Axis, FULL SAFE blocks the trigger but leaves the bolt free to lift and cycle, so a rifle on safe can still be unloaded — and can still be loaded. There is no mid position on the Axis; the button is at one end or the other. Check it works before you strip, because you will check it again after the stock goes back on.
steps.prose: That two-position design is what makes the unload above possible with the safety still on.
steps.caution: Safe blocks the trigger, not the bolt. Treat the rifle as capable of chambering a round at any time.
steps.quote: FULL SAFE - Pull safety button towards shooter (trigger blocked - bolt can be opened).
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 2, Two Position Safety, p.4

steps.title: This is the AXIS II — Section 4 is the half of the book that is yours
steps.action: Before you follow anything in this manual about the trigger, confirm which Axis you own. Savage prints the AXIS I and the AXIS II in one book and marks the division on the contents page itself: Section 4, AccuTrigger Adjustment, is flagged "(Axis II ONLY)". Your Axis II has the AccuTrigger with the bladed AccuRelease in the face of the trigger; an Axis I has a plain trigger face and no blade. If the trigger in front of you has no centre blade, you are holding an Axis I and Section 4 is not for your rifle.
steps.prose: Every other section — safety, bolt, stock, maintenance — is common to both models.
steps.caution: Section 4 is Axis II only. Identify your trigger before you touch it.
steps.quote: SECTION 4: AccuTrigger Adjustment (Axis II ONLY) SECTION 5: Parts List and Diagram SECTION 6: Ammunition Bullet Weights / Magazine Capacities SECTION 7: Rings And Bases For Mounting A Scope SECTION 8: Maintenance SECTION 9: Statement Of Limited Warranty
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Contents, p.1

steps.title: If it is an AXIS I, the trigger is not adjustable at all
steps.action: The other side of that split is a prohibition, and Savage states it twice in this manual. On an AXIS I — any Savage or Stevens without an AccuTrigger — the trigger mechanism is not adjustable, and Savage puts any post-factory adjustment squarely on the user as an unsafe-to-shoot risk. So the adjustment tool, the spring tail and the clockwise/counter-clockwise limits described later belong to the Axis II AccuTrigger and to nothing else in this book. Do not carry them across to a standard-trigger rifle because the two share a receiver profile.
steps.quote: AS WITH ANY SAVAGE OR STEVENS FIREARM NOT INCORPORATING AN ACCUTRIGGER, THE TRIGGER MECHANISM ON THE AXIS I IS NOT ADJUSTABLE. ANY ADJUSTMENTS MADE AFTER THE FIREARM LEAVES THE FACTORY MAY RENDER IT UNSAFE TO SHOOT AND IS THE SOLE RESPONSIBILITY/LIABILITY OF THE USER.
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Installing and Removing the Bolt Assembly, p.5
steps.warn: AXIS I trigger: not adjustable. Not by you, not by anyone outside the factory.

steps.title: Trigger held back, bolt release pressed — both, together
steps.action: With the safety forward at READY TO FIRE and the rifle confirmed empty, lift the bolt handle and pull the bolt fully rearward, then pull the trigger all the way back and hold it there while you press the top of the bolt release down as far as it will go. Both have to be held at once: the trigger drops the sear out of the bolt's path and the bolt release lifts the stop, and releasing either one re-traps the bolt. This is why the bolt release sits inside the trigger guard area, within reach of the same hand. Nothing here is forced — if it feels like it needs force, one of the two is not fully down.
steps.prose: Savage requires the safety forward for this, which is the opposite of the loading routine. Confirm the chamber again before you move the safety off.
steps.quote: Lift the bolt handle and pull fully to the rear. 3. WITH NO AMMUNITION IN THE FIREARM, pull the TRIGGER (1) fully rearward and hold it in that position. 4. Press down on the top of the BOLT RELEASE (2) as far as it will go.
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Bolt Removal, p.6
steps.warn: The trigger gets pulled during this procedure. The rifle must already be proved empty.

steps.title: Draw the bolt straight out of the back of the receiver
steps.action: Holding the trigger and the bolt release as above, grasp the bolt handle and pull the bolt assembly rearward until it clears the receiver ring and comes out in your hand. It should slide out level and unhurried; if it binds or stops part way, that is the sear or the bolt stop still standing in its path rather than a tight bolt. Savage names the fix precisely — trigger fully rearward first, then the bolt release pressed as far down as it will go. Let both off, start again, and it comes out.
steps.prose: Set the bolt aside on a cloth with the bolt face up. It is the one part in this strip that carries the serial match.
steps.quote: Grasping the BOLT HANDLE, pull the bolt assembly fully rearward until it clears the receiver. If it seems to bind or stop, be sure that the trigger has been pulled fully rearward first and then the BOLT RELEASE pushed as far down as it will go.
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Bolt Removal, p.6

steps.title: Read the four digits by the extractor before this bolt goes back
steps.action: Turn the bolt so the bolt head faces you and find the four digits engraved beside the extractor; they must match the last four of the serial number on the receiver. On the Axis that engraving is the factory's record that this bolt was headspaced to this barrel, and it is checked at installation rather than at removal because installation is where the wrong bolt gets fitted. Read it now while the bolt is in your hand and the receiver is in front of you. If they disagree, stop — that bolt does not belong in that rifle.
steps.prose: Savage ships Axis rifles with the bolt packed separately in the box, which is exactly how two rifles cleaned together get their bolts swapped.
steps.quote: BEFORE INSTALLING THE BOLT, VERIFY THAT THE 4 DIGITS ENGRAVED BY THE EXTRACTOR MATCH THE LAST 4 DIGITS OF THE SERIAL NUMBER ON THE RECEIVER.
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Installing and Removing the Bolt Assembly, p.5
steps.warn: Four digits by the extractor = last four of the receiver serial number. Check every time.

steps.title: An Axis bolt is matched to one rifle and no other
steps.action: Never fit a bolt from another Savage — not another Axis, not a spare from a parts bin — into this receiver. Savage states that bolt assemblies are specifically matched to a firearm, and the consequence it names is extensive damage to the rifle and serious injury to the shooter or bystanders. The mechanism behind that is headspace: on this design the bolt head and its lugs set the distance from the bolt face to the chamber shoulder, and a foreign bolt sets it wrong in one direction or the other. If the bolt is lost, the whole rifle goes back to Savage to have a new one fitted at the owner's expense.
steps.quote: BOLT ASSEMBLIES ARE SPECIFICALLY MATCHED TO A FIREARM. USING ANY OTHER BOLT ASSEMBLY MAY CAUSE EXTENSIVE DAMAGE TO THE FIREARM AND/OR SERIOUS INJURY TO THE SHOOTER OR BYSTANDER.
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 8, Cleaning and Care of Your Firearm, p.15
steps.warn: One bolt, one rifle. Never interchange.

steps.title: Magazine out before the stock comes off
steps.action: Take the detachable box magazine out and leave it out before you touch the action screws. On the Axis the magazine latch and its release tab are carried in the stock assembly, so the magazine is trapped between the stock and the action as the two separate and a magazine still in place fouls the trigger guard section coming down. Savage prints this as its own instruction ahead of the stock removal. Confirm the chamber is empty again at this point — the rifle is about to be turned upside down.
steps.quote: ALWAYS REMOVE THE DETACHABLE BOX MAGAZINE PRIOR TO REMOVING THE STOCK (SEE FIGURE 9).
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Removing the Stock, p.7

steps.title: Two action screws, 5/32-inch Allen, rifle upside down
steps.action: Turn the rifle upside down with the muzzle pointed away from you and back both action screws out with a 5/32-inch Allen wrench. They are different lengths — the longer screw is the rear one — so keep them separated as they come out rather than dropping them in one dish. Support the barrelled action with your free hand as the second screw releases, because nothing else is holding the action into the stock at that point. A wrench that feels loose in the socket is the wrong size and will round the head.
steps.prose: These two screws are also the ones you check before and after every shooting session.
steps.caution: 5/32" Allen. Longer screw is the rear one — keep them apart.
steps.quote: Using a 5/32" Allen wrench, loosen and remove the two action screws securing the stock (see FIGURE 10).
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Removing the Stock, p.7

steps.title: Trigger guard section down, then lift the stock away
steps.action: With both screws out, pull the trigger guard section straight downward and off — on the Axis it is a separate moulded piece, not part of the stock — and then lift the stock clear of the barrelled action. The guard has a locating tab at its rear that sits in a hole in the stock, so it comes off with a small rearward-to-downward motion rather than straight down against resistance. Once the stock is off, look for the recoil lug: it is a loose plate that sits in a channel in the stock and it can come away with the action or stay behind. Note where it sits now, because that is the position it has to return to.
steps.prose: This is the whole field strip. Bolt out, stock off, three pieces plus the guard and the lug.
steps.quote: Remove the trigger guard section by pulling downward (see FIGURE 11).
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Removing the Stock, p.7

steps.title: Never clean a loaded rifle, and only one rifle at a time
steps.action: Before solvent comes out, confirm once more that the chamber and magazine are empty — Savage words this as an absolute rather than a preference. And keep one rifle on the bench: two Axis rifles stripped side by side is exactly how two serial-matched bolts change places, and neither owner finds out until the rifle is closed on a live round. If a second rifle is waiting, it stays in its case with its bolt in it until this one is back together.
steps.quote: NEVER ATTEMPT TO DISASSEMBLE, CLEAN, OR OIL A LOADED FIREARM!
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 8, Cleaning and Care of Your Firearm, p.15
steps.warn: One firearm on the bench at a time — bolts are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Rod from the chamber end, out the muzzle, every stroke
steps.action: Lay the rifle horizontally with the ejection port facing down and run the correct-calibre rod in from the chamber end and out at the muzzle. With the bolt out the chamber end is open, which is the whole reason Savage has you strip before you clean — pushing a rod in at the muzzle drags fouling across the crown, and the crown is what sets the last thing the bullet touches. Port facing down means the solvent and the loosened carbon fall out of the receiver instead of pooling in it. Solvent on the brush, several passes, then patches until they come out clean.
steps.prose: Finish with one oiled patch and then one dry patch, so the bore is protected but not wet.
steps.caution: Chamber end to muzzle. Never rod an Axis from the muzzle.
steps.quote: ALWAYS STARTING FROM THE CHAMBER END, PUSH THE CLEANING ROD THROUGH THE BORE AND OUT THE MUZZLE END.
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 8, Cleaning and Care of Your Firearm, p.15

steps.title: The Axis bolt does not come apart
steps.action: Clean the bolt as one piece: wipe the body, work solvent around the bolt head, extractor and ejector, and dry it. Savage bars going further in plain words, and this is a bolt with reason behind that — the mainspring is held under compression by the bolt assembly screw at the rear, and the cocking piece pin, ejector and its retaining pin are all captive parts under load. Take the screw out on the bench and the mainspring stack leaves under its own power. Inspect the bolt head, extractor and ejector for damage or wear while it is out, and leave them where they are.
steps.prose: The parts list backs this up: the ejector, ejector spring and ejector retaining pin are listed, but there is no published order for taking them out.
steps.quote: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE BOLT ASSEMBLY.
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 8, Protecting Metal Surfaces, p.16
steps.warn: Bolt exterior only. No published teardown of an Axis bolt at any level.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You should have four things in front of you: the barrelled action, the stock, the trigger guard section with its two action screws, and the bolt — plus the recoil lug and the detachable box magazine. That is the whole of what Savage publishes as user disassembly for the Axis II. With the bolt out, do the inspection the manual asks for while you have the access: look down a clear barrel for obstructions, nicks and pitting, and run your fingers down the outside of the barrel feeling for bulges. Deep Clean covers the Axis II AccuTrigger adjustment, the interior metal surfaces, and getting the recoil lug and the action screws back correctly.
steps.prose: Nothing else on this rifle opens without a gunsmith. The trigger assembly stays in the action.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt, look down the barrel to be sure it is clear of any obstruction and that there are no signs of damage (nicks, scratches, etc.), rust, or pitting.
steps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 8, Maintenance, Timeframes, p.15

deepSteps.title: Axis II AccuTrigger — and the stock does not have to come off for it
deepSteps.action: If you are adjusting the AccuTrigger, note that Savage's Axis procedure does not require the stock to be removed at all — only the trigger guard section, pulled downward as in the strip. That is a real difference from other Savage books, where the AccuTrigger sits behind a stock that has to be lifted off first, so do not import a stock-off routine from another manual. Make sure the rifle is unloaded and the bolt is open before you begin. With the guard off, the underside of the trigger and its return spring are exposed in the stock's inletting.
deepSteps.prose: Adjusting a trigger is not part of routine cleaning. Do it deliberately, on a rifle you have proved empty, or not at all.
deepSteps.caution: Axis II only. An Axis I trigger has no adjustment and must not be touched.
deepSteps.quote: ADJUSTING THE ACCUTRIGGER DOES NOT REQUIRE THE STOCK TO BE REMOVED.
deepSteps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 4, AccuTrigger Adjustment (Axis II ONLY), p.11

deepSteps.title: The supplied tool engages the spring tail from below
deepSteps.action: Insert the AccuTrigger tool that came with the rifle up into the bottom of the trigger so its slot catches the tail of the trigger return spring. The tool is a slotted key, not a screwdriver, and it turns the whole spring rather than a screw — that is why it engages the spring's tail and why an improvised substitute slips off and bends it. Seat it fully before you apply any turn. If the spring tail is not sitting in the slot, the tool will simply skid across it.
deepSteps.quote: Insert the ACCUTRIGGER supplied tool into the bottom of the trigger as shown in FIGURE 19; engaging the spring-tail with the slot on the tool.
deepSteps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 4, AccuTrigger Adjustment (Axis II ONLY), p.11

deepSteps.title: Clockwise is heavier, counter-clockwise is lighter, and both ends are hard stops
deepSteps.action: Turn the tool clockwise to increase the pull and counter-clockwise to reduce it, and let the mechanism tell you where the ends are: the maximum is where the spring clicks as it rotates, the minimum is where you first meet resistance. Savage states that the spring must not be forced past either of those points, and forcing it is how the spring tail is bent or unhooked, leaving a trigger with no return. Go a small amount at a time and function-check between adjustments rather than running it to a stop and back. Refit the trigger guard section before any function test.
deepSteps.prose: The AccuRelease blade in the trigger face is what makes this adjustable range safe — it blocks the sear unless the blade itself is pressed squarely.
deepSteps.quote: tool clockwise. The maximum trigger pull is at the point where the spring "clicks" when rotated. 4. To adjust towards the lower range of pull, turn the tool counter-clockwise. The minimum trigger pull is at the point where you detect resistance. THE SPRING SHOULD NOT BE FORCED BEYOND THESE LIMITS.
deepSteps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 4, AccuTrigger Adjustment (Axis II ONLY), p.11
deepSteps.warn: Never force the spring beyond the click or beyond first resistance.

deepSteps.title: Do not pry at the cocking piece pin, and do not slam the bolt
deepSteps.action: While the bolt is out, look at the triangular cutout at the rear of the bolt body and leave the cocking piece pin sitting in it alone. Savage warns that cycling the bolt aggressively — slamming it back against the sear — can make the cocking piece disengage and uncock, letting the firing pin snap forward, and that deliberately prying the pin out of its recess does the same thing on purpose. There is no cleaning task on this rifle that requires the pin to be touched or moved. Wipe around it and stop; if the pin, the ejector or anything else looks weak or is not returning, the rifle goes to a gunsmith rather than back to the range.
deepSteps.quote: AGGRESSIVELY CYCLING THE BOLT (I.E. SLAMMING IT REARWARD AGAINST THE SEAR) MAY CAUSE THE COCKING PIECE TO DISENGAGE AND UNCOCK - ALLOWING THE FIRING PIN TO SNAP FORWARD.
deepSteps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Cocking Piece Pin, p.6
deepSteps.warn: Cycle the bolt deliberately. A slammed bolt can drop the firing pin.

deepSteps.title: Interior metal surfaces — the bolt is out for a reason
deepSteps.action: With the bolt already out and the stock off, this is the only state in which the inside of the receiver, the underside of the action and the recoil lug seat are reachable. Wipe foreign matter — mud, twigs, grass out of a day in the field — off with a soft cloth first, then oil what you can actually reach. Savage's instruction is explicit that the bolt comes out before cleaning and oiling precisely so that all surfaces can be got at. Do the bolt raceways in the receiver while you are there; they collect more than anything else on this rifle.
deepSteps.quote: In order to be able to reach all surfaces, remove the bolt prior to cleaning and oiling.
deepSteps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 8, Protecting Metal Surfaces, p.16

deepSteps.title: A very thin film, and no more
deepSteps.action: Oil the cleaned metal with a thin coat and then wipe the excess back off. Savage's stated standard is a very thin film and a blunt instruction not to over oil, and on this rifle the reason is under your hands: the trigger assembly sits in an open inletting under the action, and oil that runs down off the receiver collects there with powder residue and grass seed. A wet action in cold weather is also slow, which on a two-position safety and a sear is not a cosmetic problem. Rubbing is what removes rust here, not soaking.
deepSteps.prose: Excess oil also soaks into a wood or laminated stock's inletting and swells it, which moves the bedding.
deepSteps.caution: Thin film. Excess oil ends up in the trigger.
deepSteps.quote: A VERY THIN FILM OF OIL IS SUFFICIENT PROTECTION - DO NOT OVER OIL!!!
deepSteps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 8, Cleaning and Care of Your Firearm, p.16

deepSteps.title: The recoil lug goes back before the action does
deepSteps.action: Before the action drops back in, check the recoil lug is sitting correctly in its channel in the stock. It is a loose plate on this rifle, so it can fall out unnoticed while the stock is on the bench, and it is what stops the action driving rearward in the stock under recoil. Savage's position is unambiguous: if the recoil lug is misplaced or lost, the rifle is not to be used until it is replaced. Position the action so the recess in the receiver lines up perfectly with the lug before any weight goes on it.
deepSteps.prose: A lug fitted crooked or left out will not stop the action moving, and the first thing that shows up as is a group that walks.
deepSteps.quote: BE SURE THE RECOIL LUG IS STILL POSITIONED CORRECTLY IN THE STOCK (SEE FIGURE 14).
deepSteps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Removing the Stock, p.7
deepSteps.warn: No recoil lug, no shooting. Replace it before the rifle is used.

deepSteps.title: Both action screws start loose, then front first to about 40 inch pounds
deepSteps.action: Start both action screws by hand — longer to the rear, shorter to the front — and turn them only until the threads just engage the receiver, keeping the stock deliberately loose at that stage. Then, with downward pressure on the receiver to hold the recoil lug in its slot, tighten the front screw first to roughly 40 inch pounds and the rear one after it to the same. Running either screw down tight before the other is engaged pulls the action out of square in the stock and can leave the lug half-seated. Cycle the bolt several times afterwards; if the bolt handle will not close fully, the two screws are in the wrong holes.
deepSteps.prose: Check the action screws before and after every shooting session — Savage calls that good practice and it is the cheapest accuracy check there is.
deepSteps.caution: Loose first, front screw first, about 40 inch pounds each.
deepSteps.quote: Maintaining downward pressure on the receiver to be sure the recoil lug remains engaged in the receiver slot, install the action screws (longer screw is to the rear and the shorter screw is to the front) into the stock (see FIGURE 10) and turn the wrench clockwise until the threads of the screws just engage into the receiver. DO NOT OVER TIGHTEN - the stock must be loose at this step!
deepSteps.cite: SAVAGE ARMS AXIS® BOLT ACTION RIFLE — REV 4 (10/13) — printed as "108633 REV 4(10/13)" — Section 3, Installing the Stock, p.8

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Bolt out, rifle horizontal, ejection port facing down
Correct-calibre rod from the CHAMBER end, out the muzzle — never from the muzzle
Powder solvent on the brush, several passes, then clean patches until they come out clean
One patch saturated with gun oil, then one dry patch to take the excess back out
Check the bore afterwards for pieces of patch or any other obstruction

cleaning.name: BOLT ASSEMBLY (exterior only)
tasks: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE BOLT ASSEMBLY — Savage bars it outright
Wipe the body and work solvent around the bolt head, extractor and ejector
Inspect the bolt head, extractor and ejector for damage or excessive wear while it is out
Leave the cocking piece pin alone — nothing in cleaning requires it to be moved
Verify the four digits by the extractor against the last four of the receiver serial before it goes back

cleaning.name: ACTION, STOCK & RECOIL LUG
tasks: Soft cloth first for mud, twigs and grass, then a thin coat of oil on cleaned metal
Clean and lightly oil the interior metal surfaces you can reach with the bolt out
Carefully inspect the trigger assembly for damage or foreign debris with the stock removed
Confirm the recoil lug is correctly positioned in the stock channel before reassembly
Examine the stock and the studs that secure the carrying strap

cleaning.name: BENCH DISCIPLINE
tasks: One firearm on the bench at a time — Axis bolts are serial-matched and not interchangeable
Never disassemble, clean or oil a loaded firearm
Read the cautions on every solvent and chemical before use
A very thin film of oil is sufficient protection — do not over oil

reassembly: Confirm the chamber and the magazine well are empty and the bore is clear of patch material.
Set the recoil lug correctly in its channel in the stock, then lower the barrelled action in so the recess in the receiver aligns with the lug.
Fit the trigger guard section: engage its rear tab in the mating hole in the stock first, then rotate the front section into place.
Start both action screws by hand — longer to the rear, shorter to the front — until the threads just engage; the stock stays loose at this stage.
With one hand at the trigger area and one at the forend, confirm the action is bedded solidly with no rocking front-to-back or up-and-down.
Maintaining downward pressure on the receiver, tighten the front action screw to about 40 inch pounds, then the rear to about 40 inch pounds.
Rotate the front baffle to line the bolt undercut up with the extractor, pull the trigger fully rearward and hold it, press the bolt release down, and slide the bolt in with no ammunition present.
Close the bolt handle downward and verify the two position safety works in both positions.
Insert the detachable box magazine rear end first, pressing up on the front until the latch is fully engaged.
fncheck: Cycle the bolt several times and confirm it runs and locks down cleanly; if the bolt handle will not close completely, the two action screws are in the wrong holes and must be swapped. Verify the two position safety operates in both positions as described in Section 2 — full rearward covering the red dot with the trigger blocked, full forward exposing it. Look through the bore against a light and confirm there are no obstructions, including pieces of cleaning patch. Confirm the recoil lug is engaged and both action screws are secure; Savage calls checking the action screws before and after each shooting session good practice. Finally, re-read the four digits by the extractor against the last four digits of the receiver serial number — that check belongs to bolt installation, and this is bolt installation.
